series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: 1D Kohonen SOM of Δhigh/Δlow feed → open-close functor
mechanism: Competitive-learning SOM maps a multi-dimensional feed vector (Δlow−Δhigh over SCALE bars, IN_WIDTH=2*SCALE) onto a single-dimension functor (latest open−close). Training shrinks neighborhood radius and learning rate; live mapping picks BMU by Euclidean feed-error. Quantization Error (feed-error/IN_RADIUS) and Topological Error (functor-error proxy) gate map quality before the functor sign is used as a long/short weight.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURJPY; trained 2018-10-01→2021-06-01, forward thereafter; author urges large TFs first due to ~10k training iterations/bar
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an unsupervised topological compressor that turns local high/low microstructure into a 1D organized state plus explicit QE/TE quality sensors — a regime embedding that is not a supervised classifier and carries map-organization diagnostics.
quote: For a trader, if we are for the purpose of this article focus only on time-based price series, the knowns (that we’ll refer to as feed data) at any time are the prices left of that time with the unknowns (that we’ll call functor data) being those to the right. ... rather than reducing our high dimensional data to a 2D map, we will map it onto a single line.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: LDA projection of close-change features into bull/bear/whipsaw centroids
mechanism: CLDA on last-4 prepared close features (discretized / normalized-to-range / continuized / raw) with a regulizer neutral band around zero change. Labels are forward close-change classes (bullish/bearish/whipsaw). New bar projected via best eigenvector; distance to class centroids yields a signed −1…+1 regime score normalized to 0–100. Same pipeline applied to High/Low for trailing and to High−Low range for money sizing.
why_new_for_mis: Supervised class-separation axis (maximize between/within scatter) rather than max-variance PCA — directly senses bull/bear/chop regimes and also projects volatility (bar range) for size/stop sensing from the same mechanism.
quote: crucial difference between the two dimensionality reduction methods is PCA tries to find the axes with maximum variance for the whole data set ... whereas LDA tries to find the axes that actually set the data apart based on classification. ... LDA can help with initial sizing if we consider volatility or the range between High and Low prices.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Online multilayer perceptron classifier with persistent weights
mechanism: Alglib CMLPBase/CMLPTrain classifier (0–2 hidden layers) trained on column-normalized feature matrix with 2-class bullish/bearish outputs. MLPStartTraining then MLPContinueTraining preserves weights across bars instead of re-randomizing; weights are file-exported when EA criterion beats prior benchmark. MLPProcess yields long/short probabilities for signal voting.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Wizard EA backtest with walk-forward; instrument/TF not locked in prose — wizard timeframe selectable
why_new_for_mis: Continual online neural regime sensor that carries forward learned weights bar-to-bar and checkpoints them by trading criterion — a deployable sequence/regime classifier for MIS rather than a one-shot offline model.
quote: Once we start training in order not to deal with random weights all over again, we can preserve the weights learnt from the prior pass and continue training with them. The default train function always randomizes weights and if we were to use it we’d be randomizing our weights on each new bar!

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: K-means++ close-change clusters labeled by forward return
mechanism: Alglib k-means++ (SelectInitialCenters + Lloyd KMeansGenerateInternal) clusters vectors of successive close changes. Lagged forward close-change labels (y) are appended; current point’s cluster membership averages those labels and normalizes by recent high−low range to a 0–100 vote.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD daily; backtest 2022-01-01→2023-02-01, walk-forward →2023-10-01; real ticks
why_new_for_mis: Unsupervised partition of short-horizon return geometry into regimes whose forward-labeled mean gives a volatility-normalized directional sensor without presupposing linear separability.
quote: Once the ‘x’ matrix and ‘y’ array are filled with data the cluster definition proceeds ... identifying the cluster of the current close price changes ... with this sum we can easily use get the average change which when we normalize with the current range (or volatility) provides us with a weighting in the 0 – 1 range.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Fractal-wave apex sequence as k-means feature source
mechanism: Buffer of fractal indicator apex prices (high/low fractal buffers skipping DBL_MAX placeholders) accumulates until size = training_points+features+1; successive apex-to-apex changes replace raw close changes as the k-means feature vectors, then same forward-label voting.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD daily; same 2022–2023 window; required TP exits unlike close-change variant
why_new_for_mis: Senses swing/structure regime via irregularly sampled wave apexes rather than fixed-bar returns — a structural change sensor MIS can use for swing-state clustering.
quote: once we get past this we are provided with price information that is sorted in a wave like pattern. And the thesis here is the changes between each wave apex, the fractal price point, can substitute the close price changes we used in our first implementation.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Unconventional RBM: autoencoding MLP hidden state of multi-indicator vector
mechanism: 3-layer MLP with matched input/output size (5) and smaller hidden (3), trained unsupervised by setting target=input (Gibbs-sampling analogue via LM backprop). Hidden-layer neuron values (pre/post activation → size 6) are treated as the input’s probability distribution / normalized embedding. Current embedding compared to past embeddings by cosine similarity; similarity-weighted average of known forward close changes is the forecast. Inputs: MA, MACD, Stochastic, WPR, RVI.
data_needed: MA, MACD, Stoch, WPR, RVI buffers
weight file gated by cosine reconstruction loss
why_new_for_mis: Compresses a heterogeneous indicator panel into a hidden probability-distribution embedding usable as a multi-factor regime fingerprint, then retrieves analogous past states by cosine similarity — a neural sensor for cross-indicator state matching.
quote: Training objective to recap will be getting network weights that can accurately map features of input data in the hidden layer. ... These hidden neuron values can be taken as a normalization format of the 5 indicator values. ... a weighted average where cosine similarity between these vectors can act as the weight would provide the average forecast to the next change.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: DBSCAN density regimes with organic cluster count and noise tag
mechanism: DBSCAN(epsilon, min_points) over Euclidean distance of point keys; ExpandCluster/RegionQuery grow density-reachable sets; points left at cluster_id=-1 are noise. Three featureizations: (1) 4-D ΔO/ΔH/ΔL/ΔC in points, (2) RSI at 0 and cumulative lags A/B/C, (3) MA change triples. Clusters labeled by forward close change; current cluster’s mean label votes 0–100. Cluster count is discovered, not preset.
data_needed: OHLC or RSI or MA series
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD daily, year 2023; limit-order entries, no TP/SL
why_new_for_mis: Density-based regime discovery that does not require choosing k a priori and explicitly tags outliers as noise — useful for MIS when the number of market states is unknown and contamination must be sensed.
quote: With Density Based Spatial Clustering for Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) the number of clusters to be formed is a ‘respected’ unknown. ... By taking just two parameters namely epsilon ... and the number of minimum points ... DBSCAN is able to not only generate clusters from sampled data, but also determine the appropriate number of these clusters.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Support-vector hyperplane of (Δhigh, Δlow) via Newton polynomial
mechanism: 2-D features = high-change and low-change; labels = forward close up/down. Classifier screens support-vector candidates: points farther than own-set SD from own centroid and closer than cross-SD to opposing centroid. Midpoints between SVs are interpolated; Newton polynomial fits the hyperplane; query (ΔH,ΔL) side of curve gives ±100 class, optionally scaled by a proximity regressor.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURJPY daily, year 2023; real ticks, limit orders, no TP/SL
why_new_for_mis: Geometry sensor that locates the decision boundary from boundary-local support vectors in high/low-change space — a transparent 2-D regime separator MIS can use when class counts are known but shape is nonlinear.
quote: by adding a ‘classifier’ function that filters the points in each of the sets that are used in deriving the hyperplane. By considering points that are furthest from the centroid of their own set while being closest to the centroid of the opposing set, we come up with 2 subsets of points ... that can be used to interpolate the hyperplane boundary.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Bayesian posterior of next signed-change cluster given current evidence
mechanism: Close changes clustered into {neg=0, flat=1, pos=2}. For a chosen hypothesis cluster (long/short target), estimate P(E|H), P(H), P(E) from co-occurrence counts in a rolling series, then posterior P(H|E)=(P(E|H)·P(H))/P(E). Posterior>0.5 maps to a 0–100 signal. Same BI applied to consecutive trade P&L clusters for sizing and to Δ(high−low) clusters for trailing distance.
why_new_for_mis: Online belief update over discrete micro-regimes (up/flat/down or range-expand/contract) — a change-of-state probability sensor that adapts with each new bar/trade rather than a fixed classifier.
quote: our posterior probability is finding out the likelihood that a given position’s cluster type occurs next given that the latest evidence (cluster at index 0), has occurred. ... Our time series for this will have to focus on price bar range as this is always a good proxy for volatility.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Epoch-wise genetic symbolic regression of close→next-close map
mechanism: Expression trees of form (coeff, x-exponent, sign, …) grown in epochs by tree size (1…m_epochs). Within each epoch: random population → fitness via RegressionMetric(RMSE) of predicted vs actual next close → percentile prune → crossover + 5% mutation. Best tree across epochs evaluates current close to forecast next; normalized % gap → 0–100 vote.
data_needed: population, generations, fitness percentile, regressor metric
why_new_for_mis: Discovers an explainable algebraic mapping from price to next price without assuming linearity or a fixed network — a transparent change-forecast sensor whose expression tree is itself the model card.
quote: Symbolic regression allows the descriptive model that maps two data sets to be constructed as an expression tree while starting with randomly assigned nodes. ... demystifying the black box model relationship between studied data sets by introducing explainability, since the constructed expression trees inherently ‘explain’ ... how the input data actually maps to the target.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Relative CPI/inflation differential as FX regime sensor
mechanism: Economic calendar sector=prices events archived to SQLite then CSV (tester workaround). For a pair, read latest ACTUAL inflation-like prints for margin vs profit currency (e.g. GBP cpi-yy vs USD core-pce-price-index-yy). Long when margin inflation < profit inflation (weight ∝ gap/profit rate); short when reversed.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD; monthly TF aligned to monthly CPI releases
why_new_for_mis: Macro fundamental sensing layer (relative inflation) complementary to price-technical sensors — a slow regime driver MIS can fuse with faster microstructure signals.
quote: Our signal is simply generated based on the relative size of these rates. If the margin currency has a higher inflation rate than the profit currency, then we would short the pair. If, on the other hand, the inflation rate of the margin currency is less, then we would go long.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Conditional GAN close-change generator with discriminator verification
mechanism: Generator MLP maps 4 normalized prior close-changes → next change. Discriminator sees 5-tuples that are either real consecutive changes or (4 real + generated). Training alternates real/fake order; generator backprop weighted by −log(D(G(z))). At inference, DisOut confirms whether GenOut fools the discriminator; only then is |GenOut|·100 used as long/short vote.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Wizard-assembled EA test runs (FX); architecture demo with small hidden layers
why_new_for_mis: Adversarial sequence sensor: forecast plus a realism gate from a discriminator trained to spot synthetic transitions — MIS gets both a change prediction and a confidence-of-plausibility flag.
quote: the discriminator can still be used to verify the generator forecasts. If it is unable to tell they are by the generator, then it serves as confirmation that our generator network has gotten good at its job. ... GetOutput() which returns 2 things. The estimated change in close price ... and the boolean variable ‘DisOut’ which longs whether or not this change in close forecast was able to fool the discriminator network.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Pythagorean GM/HM means as low-weighted support and mirrored resistance
mechanism: AM = ordinary mean; GM = (∏x)^(1/n); HM = n/Σ(1/x). Because GM/HM overweight values near zero/lows they act as support proxies; mirrors GM'=AM+(AM−GM), HM'=AM+(AM−HM) overweight highs as resistance. HM divergence: (ΔHM'_high − ΔHM_low)>0 with confirming close change → entry. GM bands: upper = GM'(highs)+2·σ(highs), lower = GM(lows)−2·σ(lows); long on reclaim of lower band, short on loss of upper band.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURJPY M20, year 2023; also combined 3-signal weighting test
why_new_for_mis: Asymmetric mean sensors that deliberately bias toward extremes (support/resistance and band envelopes) rather than central tendency alone — useful volatility/structure envelopes for MIS without classic Bollinger symmetry.
quote: If it is just the price of securities, then the moving average could act a good proxy for support. Why? It (the GM & HM) gives greater weight to the low prices. ... By introducing mirror equivalents or reflections of GM and HM we are in a sense adding a balance ... we can now use either GM’ or HM’ as higher price weighted averages to serve as more effective proxies in defining the resistance level.
